What a signal may do, and what happens when it may not

Source: R/core-signal-gate.R
hr_signal_policy.Rd

A policy names a signal, the action it would gate and where an item goes when the signal cannot gate it. hr_apply_signal() applies it.

Usage

hr_signal_policy(
  signal,
  action,
  on_fail = c("route_check", "route_person", "ignore")
)

hr_apply_signal(sig, policy, cal = NULL, key = NULL)

Arguments

signal

The signal's name.

action

The action the signal would gate, as given to hr_gate_threshold().

on_fail

Where an item goes when the signal does not gate it: "route_check" (an outside check, the default), "route_person" or "ignore".

sig

An hr_signal from hr_signal(), or the bare value (one or more), taken to be the policy's signal.

policy

An hr_signal_policy.

cal

An hr_calibration, or NULL.

key

The run's calibration key (see hr_calibrate_signal()). Without it the record cannot be checked, and the signal stays advisory.

Value

hr_signal_policy() returns an hr_signal_policy: a list with signal, action and on_fail.

hr_apply_signal() returns a data frame with one row per value: signal, value, p (the mapped probability, or NA), threshold, gated (whether the gate decided), act (whether the action is taken), would_act (what the value alone suggests: the value of a logical signal, or p >= threshold when both are known), route ("act", or the policy's on_fail) and reason.

Details

hr_apply_signal() lets the signal gate only when every one of these holds: a calibration record is given, it is for this signal, its key matches the run's key (hr_calibration_valid()), its status is "gating", and its gate was set for the policy's action. Otherwise the signal is advisory: gated is FALSE, the action is not taken, the item is routed by on_fail, and reason says which condition failed. When the signal does gate, the action is taken for a value whose mapped probability is at or above the gate's threshold, and a value below it is routed by on_fail. No reader calls this yet, so nothing in the package gates on a signal.

See also

Other signals: hr_calibrate_signal(), hr_calibration_valid(), hr_gate_threshold(), hr_signal()

Examples

pol <- hr_signal_policy("gr.iterative.can_answer", "stop")
sig <- hr_signal("gr.iterative.can_answer", TRUE)

# With no calibration record the signal stays advisory.
hr_apply_signal(sig, pol)
#>                    signal value  p threshold gated   act would_act       route
#> 1 gr.iterative.can_answer  TRUE NA        NA FALSE FALSE      TRUE route_check
#>                  reason
#> 1 no calibration record
